styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Old lanes, temples and jasmine-tea teahouses.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Fish balls, lychee pork and street snacks.

styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Hot springs, riverside walks and green hills.

stays.why: City centre. Metro interchange, big malls and easy taxis to most sights.
Stay inside the old lanes. Walk to teahouses and historic houses; quieter at night.
Riverside district with cheaper rooms and good local food streets.
Central and green, near parks and universities. Good value with metro access.

food: Try Fuzhou fish balls (yu wan): springy balls with pork filling, in a light soup. Cheap and everywhere.
Look for lychee pork (lizhi rou) and Buddha Jumps Over the Wall soup in sit-down restaurants.
Street snacks: guo bian hu rice rolls, oyster omelette and peanut soup. Expect ¥5–20 per item.
Teahouse stop in Sanfang Qixiang: jasmine tea is the local specialty. Prices vary; check the menu first.
Night food streets near Taijiang and student areas are busy and cheap. Most stalls close before midnight.
more_time: Add a half-day for hot springs: Fuzhou is known for them. Ask your hotel for a nearby option and check prices on the day.
Swap one city day for the hills and tea country outside town. Arrange a car or join a day tour.
History fans can add a temple or old-house visit in the morning and keep the afternoon free for the riverside.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the old lanes, temples and food streets at a relaxed pace; add a night for hot springs or a hill day.

month_notes: January: cool and fairly dry, highs around 16°C. Bring a warm layer for evenings.
February: similar to January but wetter, about 10 rain days. Keep an umbrella handy.
March: mild and warming, but rain picks up to around 13 days.
April: pleasant highs near 24°C. Rain is common, so plan indoor backups.
May: warm and humid, around 16 rain days. Light rain jacket helps.
June: hot and very wet, about 20 rain days. Expect heavy showers.
July: hottest month, highs near 34°C. Go out early or after sunset.
August: hot and wet again, around 20 rain days. Sticky and humid.
September: still hot but rain eases to about 15 days.
October: comfortable highs near 26°C and fewer rainy days. A good month.
November: mild and fairly dry, highs around 22°C. Great for walking.
December: cool and dry, highs near 17°C. Pack a jacket for the evenings.

climate_guide.summary: Subtropical and humid: mild winters, hot sticky summers, and rain in most months.

items.title: Best time: October to December
items.text: Mild highs of 17–26°C and fewer rain days. Good for walking the old lanes.

items.title: Rain is common
items.text: Expect 7–20 rain days a month. June and August are the wettest. Carry a small umbrella.

items.title: Hot, humid summer
items.text: July peaks near 34°C with lows around 26°C. Plan indoor sights at midday.

items.title: Mild but cool winters
items.text: January and February highs around 16°C, lows near 8°C. A jacket is enough.

items.title: Humidity all year
items.text: Sticky from May to September. Light, breathable clothes work best.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light layers, a rain jacket or umbrella, and comfortable shoes for wet lanes and hills.

transit.best: Metro for main trips; taxis are cheap for short hops.

modes.text: Lines 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and the Binhai Express Line serve the city. Buy single tickets from machines (¥1 coins, ¥5/10/20 notes).
Buses run often for ¥1, most air conditioned, but service stops around 22:00.
Taxis are cheap: ¥10 flagfall, about ¥1.4/km, under ¥30 for most trips in town. Didi works; foreigners can sign up with a Chinese phone number and a foreign credit card.
Driving is not advised for visitors; traffic jams are common due to metro construction.
Walking is good in the old lanes and riverside areas; bikes and shared bikes suit short hops.
